In mathematical physics, the '''wave maps equation''' is a geometric [[wave equation]] that solves

:<math>D^\alpha \partial_\alpha u = 0 </math>

where <math>D</math> is a [[Connection (mathematics)|connection]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Tataru|first=Daniel|title=Rough solutions for the wave maps equation|journal=American Journal of Mathematics|date=1 January 2005|volume=127|issue=2|pages=293–377|doi=10.1353/ajm.2005.0014|citeseerx=10.1.1.631.6746|s2cid=53521030}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | zbl=1065.35199 | last=Tataru | first=Daniel | title=The wave maps equation | journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] |series=New Series | volume=41 |number=2 | pages=185–204 | year=2004 | url=http://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2004-41-02/S0273-0979-04-01005-5/S0273-0979-04-01005-5.pdf | doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-04-01005-5 | doi-access=free }}</ref>

It can be considered a natural extension of the [[wave equation]] for [[Riemannian manifolds]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tao |first=Terence |title=Wave Maps (preprint) |url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao/preprints/wavemaps.pdf |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=Department of Mathematics, UCLA}}</ref>
